working_title: Local reorganization without a transferable island-resilience rule in Antarctic penguins
core_claim: Island individuality is visible in local demographic endpoints and within-island reorganization, but static breeding-island architecture does not provide a confirmed, transferable Antarctic-wide rule for demographic resilience.

part_I_Palmer.system: five neighboring Adelie penguin breeding islands near Palmer Station, 1991-2017
part_I_Palmer.primary_phenomenon: decline accompanied by concentration among within-island breeding components
part_I_Palmer.allowed_interpretation: Regional decline has a within-island spatial-demographic architecture; breeders become progressively concentrated as island populations contract.

detectable_effect.interpretation: The study had little detection probability for a common interaction around 0.30 but would usually detect a very large common interaction around 0.50-0.55. This is not an equivalence test.

radius_diagnostic.decision: Do not call the radius reversal an ecological scale-dependence discovery; report sensitivity/instability compatible with the block-permutation null.

part_II_Antarctic.observation_timing: Exact-date and <=14-day image-offset calibrations preserve all three negative primary gamma_AH signs and the chinstrap/gentoo point-estimate crossover classification.
part_II_Antarctic.scale_trait_sensitivity: The point-estimate interaction weakens at 1 km, reverses at 5 km, and is partly metric-dependent; none of these sensitivity variants replaces the frozen primary analysis.

integrated_conclusion: Local within-island reorganization is strongly supported.
A transferable macroecological buffering rule based on static island architecture is not supported.
The Paper 2 null is informative against very large common effects but not against moderate effects of the observed magnitude.
Apparent spatial-radius reversal is not unusual enough under the frozen joint null to be treated as biological scale dependence.
Local ecological organization can be real at one hierarchical level without being transportable information at another.
prohibited_claims: Island architecture generally buffers Antarctic penguin populations.
A general option-fragmentation crossover is established across Pygoscelis.
The 1/2/5 km reversal proves ecological scale dependence.
The Paper 2 null proves the true interaction is zero or smaller than MDE80.
Species-wide latent forcing identifies a specific climate mechanism.
Process-SD differences have an ecological interpretation.
Palmer and Antarctic-wide datasets are pooled as if they were one homogeneous analysis.

manuscript_structure.part_I: Palmer discovery: common decline, divergent local endpoints, within-island concentration
manuscript_structure.bridge: Does local island organization scale into a transferable predictor of resilience?
manuscript_structure.part_II: Antarctic-wide confirmatory test: negative/non-confirmatory interaction, unsupported simple buffering
manuscript_structure.diagnostic_close: MDE shows limits of the null; radius null shows apparent scale reversal is not established biologically
manuscript_structure.discussion: hierarchical information: local reorganization without macroecological transportability

odsp_role: Intellectual origin only: apparent island information can belong to species, regional, island, or within-island levels. ODSP terminology need not appear in the manuscript.
